$comment: Everyday stories, noun Experience, one part (experience, backOffice, appShellNavItem, guidePage, guidePageGadget, guidePageRegion, guidePageRegions, guidePageTheme). Same style rules as stories-pilot.json. Owner reviews each part.

stories.appShellNavItem.group: A back-office menu with thirty entries is a wall of words. Group is the section title an entry is filed under, such as 'Operations', so related entries sit together under one heading.
stories.appShellNavItem.label: The menu entry should read 'Customers', not the technical name of a concept. Label is the text shown for this entry.
stories.appShellNavItem.target: A menu entry has to lead somewhere. Target names the concept or panel it opens. An entry with no target is only a heading for a group.
stories.backOffice.defaultRoute: Staff open the back office every morning and always go to the orders first. Default route names the concept or panel that is shown when the app loads, instead of simply the first one in the list.
stories.backOffice.locale: A Brazilian company labels its back office as pt-BR. Locale is that tag, kept for information. It does not translate anything by itself, because the strings keyword is what actually changes texts.
stories.backOffice.navigation: The default menu lists every concept in the order it was declared, which is rarely the order people think in. Navigation declares the entries yourself, in display order and with groups. If you leave it out, the default menu is used.
stories.backOffice.pages: The back office can open on a start page with tiles, charts and a list of recent items, like a noticeboard. Pages are those guide pages. A concept or panel can point at one, and a pack may bring its own.
stories.backOffice.strings: The platform says 'Save' and a company would rather say 'Confirm'. Strings replaces some of the platform's fixed texts by their ids. Any text you do not list keeps the platform's English default.
stories.experience.admin: Besides the screens for each kind of worker, the company needs one back office for operators. Admin turns this entry into that back office, with its language, text changes, start route, grouped menu and guide pages. There is at most one per model.
stories.experience.backOffice: A manager mostly uses the manager screens, but sometimes needs the operators' back office. Back office, when true, adds a link to the generated back office in this experience. The back office itself is set up in its own block.
stories.experience.device: A driver uses the app on a phone, while the office clerk uses it on a desktop. Device picks web, mobile or both. Mobile means a phone-first layout with a tab bar at the bottom, at most five entries, and the app can be installed on the phone.
stories.experience.home: When a courier opens the app, the first thing they should see is today's deliveries. Home names the screen shown first.
stories.experience.name: Each kind of user gets its own address, such as one for drivers and one for managers. Name is the last piece of that address, written in lower case with dashes, and the experience is served there.
stories.experience.navigation: The driver's app needs a few tabs at the bottom: Deliveries, Map, Profile. Navigation lists those entries, each with the screen it opens, a label, an icon and, if you like, a badge. On a phone there can be at most five.
stories.experience.theme: The drivers' app should have the dark look that is easy on the eyes at night. Theme names one of the app's ready-made looks. If you say nothing, the app's own look is used.
stories.experience.title: The browser tab and the top of the app should say 'Driver app', not a code name. Title is the text shown for this experience.
stories.guidePage.default: When someone opens the back office, one guide page should already be in front of them. Default, when true, marks this page as the one shown by default.
stories.guidePage.gadgets: A guide page is a noticeboard, and a gadget is one thing pinned on it: a big number, a chart, a list of recent items. Gadgets are those pieces.
stories.guidePage.name: A start page needs a name that concepts and panels can point to, such as 'Sales'. Name is that handle.
stories.guidePage.regions: A guide page can have a column on the left, one on the right and a strip on top around the gadgets. Regions say which of them are shown.
stories.guidePage.theme: The sales page can wear the company colours. Theme holds the look of the page: accent colour, spacing, colour mode and logo.
stories.guidePageGadget.name: Two gadgets on one page must not be confused. Name is the gadget's own name, unique on the page.
stories.guidePageGadget.query: A gadget showing 'orders per week' needs numbers from somewhere. Query names the query that feeds a number tile, a chart or a table.
stories.guidePageGadget.series: A chart of sales per month becomes more useful when each region is a line of its own. Series names the query column that splits a chart into several series.
stories.guidePageGadget.title: A big number alone means little, so the tile says 'Orders waiting' above it. Title is the heading of the gadget.
stories.guidePageGadget.type: A page can show recent items, information about where the person is, a fragment of a page written by hand, a big number, bars, a line, a doughnut or a table. Type picks which of the eight a gadget is.
stories.guidePageGadget.url: A company wants a short notice from its intranet on the start page, such as 'The warehouse is closed on Friday'. Url is the address, inside the same site, of a ready-made piece of page. It is fetched and shown without running any scripts in it.
stories.guidePageGadget.x: In a chart of sales per month, the months go along the bottom. X names the query column used for those categories.
stories.guidePageGadget.y: In the same chart, the height of each bar is the amount sold. Y names the query column used for the values of a chart or a number tile.
stories.guidePageRegion.collapsible: A side column takes room that a clerk sometimes needs for the gadgets. Collapsible, when true, lets the person fold that region away.
stories.guidePageRegion.defaultCollapsed: Some people never use the side column. Default collapsed, when true, makes the region start folded, and whoever wants it can open it.
stories.guidePageRegion.enabled: The right-hand column is not needed on this page. Enabled, when true, shows the region, and when false it is not shown.
stories.guidePageRegion.width: A side column that is too wide pushes the gadgets aside. Width sets how wide the region is.
stories.guidePageRegions.left: A guide page can have a column on its left side, and not every page wants one. Left holds the settings of that region, such as whether it is shown and how wide it is.
stories.guidePageRegions.right: The same goes for a column on the right side of the page. Right holds the settings of that region, such as whether it is shown and whether it can be folded.
stories.guidePageRegions.top: A page can have a strip across the top, above the gadgets. Top, when true, shows that region.
stories.guidePageTheme.accent: A company's pages should show its own colour on buttons and highlights. Accent is that colour of the page.
stories.guidePageTheme.density: Someone who reads many rows a day wants them packed tightly, while a casual visitor prefers more air. Density sets the spacing of the page.
stories.guidePageTheme.logoText: A small company has no logo picture, only its name. Logo text is the text shown in the place of a logo.
stories.guidePageTheme.logoUrl: A company wants its logo in the corner of the page. Logo URL is the address of that picture.
stories.guidePageTheme.mode: Some people work in a bright office, others in a dim warehouse. Mode sets the colour mode of the page.
